drivers.title: No way out and no notice period either
drivers.explain: Two protections are missing at once: the document neither explains how you end the arrangement nor how much notice you must give. Together they leave the timing of your exit entirely to the other side.
drivers.askYourLawyer: With neither an exit clause nor a notice period written down, what are my rights to end this and on what terms?

drivers.title: No way out is written into the document
drivers.explain: Nothing in this document explains how you end the arrangement. An agreement with no exit written into it is one you can only leave by negotiating from a weak position.
drivers.askYourLawyer: On what terms can I end this agreement, and what does ending it cost me?

statute.section: Section 28(b), read with section 28(a) — Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void
statute.text: Every agreement, (a) by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights; or (b) which extinguishes the rights of any party thereto, or discharges any party thereto from any liability, under or in respect of any contract on the expiry of a specified period so as to restrict any party from enforcing his rights, is void to that extent.

enforceability.plainMeaning: A clause that gives you only thirty or ninety days to raise a claim, or that says your rights disappear after a short period, does not usually take away the time the general law of limitation gives you.
caveats: This describes the section, not your contract. Whether a particular clause falls inside it is for a court to decide.
Clause (b) was added by the 1997 amendment; decisions from before 1997 that upheld clauses extinguishing rights on expiry pre-date that change.
The section does not extend the time the Limitation Act gives you. That clock runs from when your cause of action arose, whatever the contract says.
Arbitration clauses that set a period for commencing arbitration are treated separately and are not all caught by this section.

statute.text: A complaint ... may be filed with a District Commission by (c) one or more consumers, where there are numerous consumers having the same interest, with the permission of the District Commission, on behalf of, or for the benefit of, all consumers so interested. ... The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of the provisions of any other law for the time being in force.

enforceability.plainMeaning: The consumer law itself allows one or more consumers to complain on behalf of many others with the same interest, with the commission's permission. A term in the contract does not remove a right the statute gives.
caveats: This describes the statutory right. Whether a group of consumers has the same interest is decided by the commission when it gives permission.
The Act applies only to consumer transactions, so a waiver in a business-to-business contract is not answered by this row.
A waiver may still matter in arbitration or in a civil suit, which are different forums with different rules.
Permission under this clause is asked for at the time of filing; it is not automatic.

statute.text: "unfair contract" means a contract ... having such terms which cause significant change in the rights of such consumer, including the following, namely: (iv) entitling a party to the contract to terminate such contract unilaterally, without reasonable cause; (vi) imposing on the consumer any unreasonable charge, obligation or condition which puts such consumer to disadvantage.

enforceability.plainMeaning: A term letting the other side change or end the deal on its own, or putting an unreasonable condition on you, is the kind of term the Act names as unfair and a consumer commission can examine.
caveats: The listing describes a category. Whether this clause falls in it, and what follows, is for a consumer commission to decide.
Only the State or National Commission can declare a contract term null and void as unfair.
Continuing to use a service after terms change is often argued as acceptance; that argument is fought on the facts and is not settled by this row.
The Central Consumer Protection Authority can also act against unfair trade practices; that is a separate route from a complaint about your own contract.

forum.name: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
forum.handles: Defective goods, deficient services, unfair trade practices and unfair contract terms, for anything bought for personal use.

portal.name: e-Jagriti, which took over consumer e-filing from e-Daakhil on 1 January 2025

fee.summary: Nothing is payable where the claim is up to Rs 5,00,000, and Rs 200 from Rs 5,00,001 to Rs 10,00,000, under rule 7 of the Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020 as amended in 2023.

forum.filingPlace: s.34(2)(d) — where you ordinarily reside or personally work for gain. A clause in the contract naming another city's courts does not displace it.
entitlements: s.39 lets the Commission order the defect removed, the goods replaced, the price refunded, compensation paid, or an unfair contract term discontinued.
s.2(46) defines an unfair contract by six limbs, including a penalty disproportionate to the loss and a right to terminate unilaterally without reasonable cause.
caveats: A complaint lies for goods or services obtained for personal use. s.2(7) excludes anything obtained for resale or for a commercial purpose, and a contract of personal service is outside the definition of service in s.2(42).
Whether what happened is a defect or a deficiency is for the Commission to decide on the evidence.
Fee slabs are set by rules that change. Confirm the current fee on the portal before filing.

limitationRule.causeOfAction: The date on which the cause of action arose — the defect, the deficiency in service or the unfair trade practice — not the date the agreement was signed.

forum.name: Grievance Appellate Committee
forum.handles: Appeals against what a social-media or other intermediary decided on your complaint — account suspension, content taken down, content left up, and privacy grievances.
forum.statute: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, rules 3(2) and 3A
forum.filingPlace: Online. The appeal is filed, heard and decided digitally, so there is nowhere to travel to.

prerequisites.step: Complain to the intermediary's Grievance Officer first. Rule 3(2)(a) requires an acknowledgement within twenty-four hours and resolution within fifteen days, and within seventy-two hours for most removal requests.

entitlements: Rule 3A(3) — an appeal lies to the Committee within thirty days of the Grievance Officer's communication, and since the 2023 amendment also where the Officer did not resolve the complaint.
Rule 3A(4) — the Committee is to endeavour to resolve the appeal within thirty calendar days, and the intermediary must comply with its order and report compliance.
caveats: The Committee reviews what the Grievance Officer decided. It is not a route for a money claim.
Rule 3A does not take away the right to go to a court instead.
Personal-data complaints under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 go to the Data Protection Board as its provisions are brought into force. Check which route is open before filing.

limitationRule.causeOfAction: The date the Grievance Officer's decision is received, or the date the fifteen days the Officer had to resolve the complaint expire.
limitationRule.statute: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, rule 3A(3)

forum.name: District or State Legal Services Authority
forum.handles: Free legal advice, drafting and representation by a panel advocate for anyone within s.12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
forum.statute: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, ss.12 and 13

fee.summary: Free, including court fees, process fees and the panel advocate, for anyone eligible under s.12.

forum.filingPlace: At the District Legal Services Authority in your district court complex, which accepts walk-in applications, or online through the NALSA portal.
entitlements: s.12(c) and s.12(f) entitle every woman, every child and every industrial workman to free legal services irrespective of what they earn.
s.12(h) entitles a person whose annual income is below the ceiling their State has fixed, and Rs 5,00,000 applies to Supreme Court matters.
Tele-Law connects you to a panel lawyer free of charge through a Common Service Centre or the Tele-Law app (tele-law.in), which is offered in 22 languages.
caveats: Eligibility is decided by the Authority on the application and the documents filed with it.
Applying for free legal aid does not stop the limitation period for the underlying claim from running.

forum.name: Lok Adalat
forum.handles: Settlement by consent of a pending case or of a dispute before any case is filed, organised by the Legal Services Authority.
forum.statute: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, ss.19 to 22B

fee.summary: Free, and s.21 refunds the court fee already paid when a pending case is settled.

forum.filingPlace: Through the District Legal Services Authority, which publishes the dates of the National Lok Adalat held each quarter.
entitlements: s.21 — an award of a Lok Adalat is deemed to be a decree of a civil court, is final, and no appeal lies against it.
s.21(1) proviso — the court fee paid in a pending case is refunded when the matter is settled in a Lok Adalat.
s.22B — a Permanent Lok Adalat hears public utility service disputes up to Rs 1,00,00,000 and may decide the matter on merits if no settlement is reached.
caveats: A Lok Adalat records a settlement both sides agree to. Apart from a Permanent Lok Adalat under s.22C, it decides nothing by itself.
Because an award is final and no appeal lies from it, what is agreed there cannot later be reopened.
Waiting for a Lok Adalat date does not stop the limitation period for filing from running.
